title: Compact-series-mode: tokenized tooltips, aria-live batching, and GPU-fallback layout
creator: Priya Shah
description: Introduce a compact-series display mode to reduce DOM and paint overhead for high-density time-series charts. This ticket covers: a tokenized tooltip lifecycle (pre-baked tooltip tokens reused across series), batching aria-live announcements to avoid screen reader spam, and a GPU-fallback layout path for browsers where canvas-accelerated layering yields significant paint cost reductions. Goal: reduce mean-frame work for dense charts by 30-50% while preserving keyboard/AT semantics and legend discoverability.
acceptance_criteria: Compact-series mode available as a config flag on TimeSeriesChart component
Tooltip tokens reused across visible series; tooltip creation/destruction rate reduced by >=60% in benchmark harness
Aria-live announcements batched and debounced to max 1 announcement per 400ms during scrubbing
Legend items maintain keyboard focus order and expose 'focused-series' aria attribute for ATs
GPU-fallback layout demonstrated in Canary with >25% reduction in main-thread CPU for 10k-point series
Design review completed and accessibility review signed off
Unit and integration tests for tooltip lifecycle and aria batching added
Migration notes and examples added to design system docs and component changelog
changes: 2026-03-02: Drafted proposal and initial sketches; performance hypothesis: reuse tooltip DOM + batch aria causing 30-50% CPU reduction on dense datasets.
2026-03-04: Spike implemented by ENG to measure DOM create/destroy cost on Chrome; observed ~70% tooltip lifecycle ops reduction when tokenized.
2026-03-06: Design review with PM and Eng; decided to implement aria-live batching at 400ms to balance immediacy and AT noise. PM flagged customer-facing behavior for scrubbing speed.
2026-03-09: Accessibility review scheduled; vendor AT consultant suggested explicit role attributes for legend items and a live region summarizer for aggregated updates.
2026-03-11: Engineering prototype of GPU-fallback layout (CSS will-change + canvas layering) shows 28% main-thread improvement for 5 simultaneous series with 8k points each.
2026-03-13: Updated designs to include 'compact legend mode'—inline mini-sparkline + truncated label with reveal on keyboard focus. Added microcopy for discovery.
2026-03-14: Began implementation PR; added tests stubs and example story. Blocking: finalize analytics event schema for tooltip impressions.
design_notes: Tokenized tooltip model: create a small set of tooltip DOM nodes (3-5) reused for all visible series. Tooltips are populated from a lightweight token object instead of recreating DOM per hover event.

Aria batching: accumulate semantic updates for scrubbing and release a summarized announcement when user stops for >= 400ms. For rapid scrubbing, expose a concise live region message like '3 series, point values updated'.
Legend semantics: each legend item receives aria-controls linking to the chart canvas and aria-pressed when toggled. Keyboard focus should jump to reveal full label and mini-sparkline expansion.

GPU-fallback: use layered canvas approach where static series render to offscreen canvas textures and active layers (hover, annotations) remain as separate layers to minimize repaints. Fallback will opt into CSS compositing and will-change hints only after feature detection.
Performance testing harness: use Storybook story with synthetic datasets (1k, 5k, 10k points) and Lighthouse / custom perf tracing to capture main-thread and paint metrics.
Tradeoffs: Tokenized tooltips reduce accessibility granularity if not carefully composed; ensure each batch announcement contains clear context and allow a user preference to disable batching.
Rollout plan: feature-flagged in design system v-next, opt-in in Console routes with telemetry, then toggle on by default after 2 weeks of metrics validation.
